interpretation: Local detail scene, not a measured map tile. Rock forms, fall height, viewpoint, color and proportions are artistic choices. The river divides at the cataract into two branches. Water is hidden in the dry state; fine sand covers the upper course. Restoration brings a full upstream river, grassy banks, woods and flowering underbrush.

prompts.restored:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a large, explorable landscape illustration for the cataract detail view of an interactive atlas of George MacDonald's Lilith.
Primary request: Paint the restored Great Cataract and the river's two branches as a beautiful, believable terrain study. This is a landscape, without any interface or lettering.
Scene: A deep broad river arrives across a grassy upper plain and grassy banks, then drops sheer over a rugged rocky scarp, dividing into exactly two branches as it falls. Two substantial foaming chutes pass to either side of a rocky shoulder, and continue downstream in two distinct winding channels toward the lower left and lower right edges. The channels do not rejoin. The upper river comes from beyond the scene, not a spring. Fresh moss at the cliff foot, lush grass, flowering underbrush and irregular woodland on the margins. Keep the two branches and the cliff legible amid rich natural detail.
Composition: Wide landscape, approximately 3:2. Elevated oblique aerial view, looking across and down onto the rock face: upper river visible in the top third, cataract and fork centered, downstream branches visible in the lower third. Compact local scene; no sky or horizon. The complete fall must remain visible in the central 55 percent so it survives narrower viewport crops. Natural, asymmetrical geology, not a symmetric Y diagram. Tangible relief and believable erosion.
Style/medium: Exquisite hand-painted literary fantasy atlas; luminous gouache and oil-glaze depth, soft watercolor atmosphere, fine botanical brushwork and mineral textures. Painterly rather than photographic or game-rendered. Rich layered detail rewards zooming; elegant and quiet, not kitsch. No black contour outlines, no flat vector shapes.
Lighting/mood: Radiant, almost inwardly luminous morning light, delicate mist and reflected light in the foam; restrained wonder.
Palette: Malachite, moss and olive greens, slate blue river, creamy white falling water, warm grey and ochre rock, subtle gold light. Avoid neon cyan.
Constraints: Exactly one upstream river and two downstream branches; divide at the fall itself. No buildings, ruins, bridges, people, animals, mountains, text, labels, borders, compass, scale bar, watermark or invented landmarks. The book gives no dimensions: use coherent local proportions without claiming measured geography. Output a full painted landscape with no transparent margins.
prompts.dry:
Use case: lighting-weather
Asset type: dry-state companion illustration for the same explorable cataract scene in a literary atlas.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target, the restored Great Cataract. Keep its viewpoint, dimensions, crop, exact rocky scarp silhouette, central rocky shoulder, both fall locations and two downstream channel alignments fixed. It must look like the SAME place before its water returned.
Primary request: Transform this landscape into the ancient dried cataract described in chapter XVI of George MacDonald's Lilith.
Changes: Remove ALL visible flowing water, waterfalls, foam, pools, spray and mist from BOTH falls and both lower channels. Expose the beautifully eroded, vertically scored rock face and rounded stones of the empty riverbeds. The upper river and ALL upper green plain become a dreary, uninterrupted expanse of the finest pale ochre sand: powdery drift fills the former upper river course level with the desert. No river groove left above the lip. Upper bank trees and flowering thickets disappear into sand, with only a few sparse dry grasses by the rocks. Lower gorge is arid stone and muted earth with sparse vegetation, but retain a lush soft green carpet of moss in sheltered pockets at the foot of the cliff, suggesting hidden water underneath the stones. Two dry channels remain separate and readable below the old waterfall.
Style and lighting: Preserve the exquisite painterly oil/gouache detail, luminous mineral surfaces, softness and subdued literary atmosphere. Late dusk: dusky lavender shadows, warm fading light on rock, pale sand, concentrated deep moss green below. Rich and beautiful in its stillness, never a generic orange desert.
Invariants: Exactly the same viewpoint and rock masses. No alteration of the fork topology. No new buildings, objects, people, animals, mountains, sky, text, labels, frames or watermark. No visible trickle: the book's water is heard hidden below. Full bleed painting, no transparency.
